items.title: Implement snapshot_freshness function in drift.py
items.why_now: The freshness contract is referenced in drift.py but no implementation exists; without it, the drift gate cannot verify snapshot freshness, leaving a gap in the architecture drift detection. This blocks the first end-to-end vertical slice.

steps.do: Add snapshot_freshness function that computes freshness of a snapshot (e.g., compare timestamps or git diff) and returns a boolean or raises if stale.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'snapshot_freshness' daedalus/ returns at least one definition; run unit test for drift module passes.

steps.do: Update the drift gate to call snapshot_freshness and fail when snapshot is stale.
steps.verified_by: Integration test: stale snapshot causes gate failure; fresh snapshot passes.

items.assumption: The full drift.py file does not already contain snapshot_freshness; confirmed by grep.

items.title: Ensure candidate error state propagation after evaluation exception
items.why_now: If evaluate() catches an exception and does not set candidates to error state, the picker may receive incomplete data, violating its 'never raises' contract. This is a medium-severity issue that could cause silent failures in candidate selection.

steps.do: Inspect evolution.py lines 155-158 to verify if candidates are set to an error state after exception. If not, add logic to mark the candidate as failed.
steps.verified_by: Code review shows error state assignment; unit test: exception during evaluation sets candidate error flag.

steps.do: Verify picker.build_queue does not depend on candidate state that could be incomplete. If it does, add defensive checks.
steps.verified_by: Code review confirms picker handles error state gracefully; integration test: candidate with error does not crash picker.

items.assumption: The cited lines exist and contain the exception handling; if not, locate the actual catch block.

items.title: Verify docref_gate aggregation exclusivity and update documentation if needed
items.why_now: If docref_gate's aggregate metrics are used in the evaluation pipeline, the claim that _by_provenance is the only aggregation path is false, causing confusion for developers and potential duplicate aggregation.

steps.do: Search for 'docref_gate' in harness.py to see if its results are consumed by eval pipelines.
steps.verified_by: grep -rn 'docref_gate' daedalus/mapping/harness.py returns results; code review determines if consumed.

steps.do: If docref_gate results are consumed by _by_provenance or other eval aggregators, update docstring to clarify exclusivity scope.
steps.verified_by: Docstring updated; code review confirms accuracy.

items.assumption: The grep will find relevant usage; if not, the exclusivity claim may still be correct but needs confirmation.

items.title: Inspect picker.py error handling for silent degradation
items.why_now: If _load_baseline or _run_eval_gate catch all exceptions and return error strings that are ignored, candidates may be selected without proper evaluation, leading to degraded assertions.

steps.do: Inspect picker.py for try/except blocks around _load_baseline and _run_eval_gate calls; verify error handling does not silently ignore failures.
steps.verified_by: Code review shows appropriate error propagation or logging; unit test: mock failure causes picker to raise or skip candidate.

steps.do: If silent degradation is found, add error propagation or logging to ensure failures are visible.
steps.verified_by: Integration test: candidate with failed eval is not selected or error is reported.

items.assumption: The functions _load_baseline and _run_eval_gate exist in picker.py; if not, locate the actual error handling.
